clue.text: Salvage extremely rare celestial object

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, so only the first and last letters of the next two words are wanted

parts.note: the two ends of the word rare
the two ends of the word celestial
an object is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Someone recovering a rare meteorite or other heavenly body that has fallen to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celestial object' reads as one thing, a star or comet, but 'extremely' trims celestial too and object stands alone as a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to recover or rescue it from loss, which is what salvaging means.

clue.text: Split over irregular decree that's basically worthless

definitions.note: adjective phrase for a noun: something worth no more than this

indicators.note: over means covering, so the first word goes round the other

parts.note: rent is the past tense of rend, to split

indicators.note: irregular is read as not-even, so the odd-numbered letters of the following word are kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of decree

explanation.surface: A divided ruling on a chaotic decree that has no real value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' picks the odd-numbered letters. A red cent is American slang for a one-cent coin, the smallest sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Not worth a red cent means worthless; the coin is the US penny, the smallest unit of value.

clue.text: Church is smart shifting this festival

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

indicators.note: shifting means moving around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The church gets smartened up for the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' signals that the festival is the answer itself, built from CH plus a rearranged IS SMART.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the Christian festival celebrating the birth of Jesus.

clue.text: Sit up after a tale from him, perhaps

definitions.note: the definition shares its opening a with the wordplay

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the other one

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: An instruction to sit up straight after hearing a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The a does double duty, starting both the wordplay and the definition; the fabulist is the man who tells such tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the ancient Greek storyteller credited with the fables, so a fable is a tale from him.

clue.text: Desperate men head to addiction treatment

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild and frantic, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Desperate men make for a clinic to get help with their dependency.
explanation.definitionFit: Methadone is a synthetic opioid prescribed as a substitute in treating heroin dependency.

clue.text: Look after the issue for others

definitions.text: Look after the issue for others

parts.words: Look after the issue for others
parts.note: surface reading: deal with a problem or matter on somebody else's behalf
setter's reading: issue means offspring, so this is minding other people's children

explanation.surface: Someone handling a matter on behalf of colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a problem or topic, but in its legal sense it means children, and minding other people's children is the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby-sitting is caring for children while their parents are away, and issue is a formal word for offspring.

clue.text: Two insects left out? That's powerful

indicators.note: out means removed, so the named letter is dropped

parts.note: a bee and a fly
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Two bugs have been ignored, which someone calls a strong move.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy describes someone muscular and strong, so powerful in build.

clue.text: Reconsider second exercise over youngster getting upset

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the earlier pieces sit above the later one

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
PE is physical education

indicators.note: upset means knocked upside down, and in a down clue that runs the word backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A coach rethinks a second training session after a boy becomes distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To back-pedal is to retreat from a position one has taken, rethinking it under pressure.

clue.text: Take time to get in close

indicators.note: to get in means to enter, so this letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: to seal is to close up
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone advised to be patient before moving in close.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal is to take something that does not belong to you.

clue.text: Attempt to give fitting advice when clothes shopping

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to try one's luck, chancing an attempt at getting away with something
second meaning: what a shop assistant says about a garment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' means both appropriate and to do with the fitting room, which is where the advice is given.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying it on means chancing an attempt at something cheeky, and also putting a garment on to check the fit.

clue.text: Diving attacker received trivial sum, initially for throwing game

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the preceding words in turn

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A dive-bombing raider is paid a pittance, a scene of warfare or perhaps a footballer taking a dive.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is the pub game in which players throw small pointed missiles at a board.

clue.text: Endeavour to capture contact linked to English betrayal

indicators.note: to capture is to hold something inside, so one word is placed within another

parts.note: to endeavour is to try

indicators.note: linked to says two pieces are joined end to end, one after the other

parts.note: to contact someone is to reach them
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An attempt to get in touch with someone, tied to an act of English treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: The contact and English pieces are joined first, and the endeavour word then wraps round the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is the act of betraying trust, so it is a synonym of betrayal.

clue.text: Pee twice, say, when going off — it's that simple

definitions.note: the answer used as an exclamation

indicators.note: going off suggests something exploding or turning bad, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
the word say written twice

explanation.surface: A cheeky childish remark about relieving oneself, said to be no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' looks attached to Pee but it doubles say; together PEE, SAY and SAY supply the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-peasy is a childish exclamation meaning something is very easy, exactly what 'it's that simple' says.

clue.text: Plan to gather information for show trial

indicators.note: to gather is to collect something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a plot is a scheme or plan
I is the abbreviation for information, as on tourist signs

explanation.surface: Planning to collect evidence for a staged political trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show trial' suggests a Stalinist courtroom, but here it is a trial run of a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a test episode made to see whether a television series is worth commissioning.

clue.text: Lure agency worker to join top table

indicators.note: to join means one piece is attached to the end of another

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker supplied by an agency

indicators.note: top refers to the head of the following word, in this case its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of table

explanation.surface: Persuading a temporary staffer to sit at the top table at a function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top table' looks like the head table at a wedding, but it means the top letter of table.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt is to entice or attract someone, the same as to lure them.

clue.text: Arrange dates here in the Middle East

definitions.note: a location phrase standing for a place there

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in a new order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to fix appointments for a trip to the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Sea lies between Africa and Arabia, a body of water in the Middle East.

clue.text: Investigator locates married American friends in Arab country

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the following word

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
buds, short for buddies, is American for friends
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A detective tracks down a married couple's American friends in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: The friends and married pieces go together inside the country, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official appointed to investigate complaints against organisations.

clue.text: Cheers when getting to the end of the drink

indicators.note: of here links two pieces placed one after the other

parts.note: the bottom is the end of something
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A drinker raises a toast on reaching the dregs of the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottoms up is a drinking toast, used just like cheers when glasses are raised.

clue.text: Bedding edge will do for mother, they say

definitions.note: verb phrase: a matricide is the one who will do for mother

indicators.note: they say means as people pronounce it, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: the edge of a mattress, which is bedding

explanation.surface: A mattress border will be fine for Mum, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do for' is British slang for kill; the sound match is approximate and its indicator sits at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Matricide is the killing of one's own mother, or the person who kills her.

clue.text: Spread discharge — it's all over now

parts.note: paste is a spread, as for sandwiches
to vent is to discharge or let out

explanation.surface: An ointment is applied to a weeping wound, and the trouble is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A past event is something that has already happened and finished, so it is all over now.

clue.text: Pools found on embankment at historic conference site

indicators.note: found on means sitting above, so in a down clue the first piece goes on top

parts.note: a pot is a pool of money, as in a jackpot
a dam is an embankment holding back water

explanation.surface: Pools of water lie on a bank beside a famous meeting place.
explanation.definitionFit: Potsdam, near Berlin, hosted the 1945 conference where the Allies decided post-war Germany's future.

clue.text: Key type added on to register

indicators.note: the answer with on added makes the next word, so on must be taken away from it

parts.note: to latch on is to grasp or register an idea

explanation.surface: A sort of key attached to a cash register or a list.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: answer plus ON gives 'latch on', meaning to register or understand, so ON comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: A latchkey is the key that opens a door latch, so latch names that type of key.

clue.text: Communication equipment created by worker group

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Telecom gear made by a team of workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A handset is the part of a telephone held in the hand, a piece of communication equipment.

clue.text: Piece in cited literature about accent

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the found letters are read the other way
a piece in something is a fragment of it, so the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: the letters straddling the end of cited and the start of literature

explanation.surface: A passage in quoted texts discussing pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is the wavy mark over letters like the n in Spanish señor, loosely called an accent.

clue.text: Material name added to charge

indicators.note: added to is read as put into, so the letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: a lien is a legal charge on property
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A fabric with the brand name adding to its price.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a cloth woven from flax, a type of material.

clue.text: Plenty in favour of merger

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a fusion is a merger or joining together

explanation.surface: Lots of support for a corporate merger.
explanation.definitionFit: A profusion is an abundance or large quantity of something, much like plenty.

clue.text: Hesitate when seeing father sitting on facility

indicators.note: sitting on means placed above, so in a down clue this piece comes first

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
facility can mean use, as in having the use of something

explanation.surface: Someone holds back on seeing Dad on the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facility' suggests a toilet, which makes the surface comic.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause is to stop briefly or hesitate before carrying on.

clue.text: Core of county police force not satisfied

indicators.note: the core is the centre, so only the middle letters of the next word are wanted

parts.note: the two central letters of county
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Rural police officers are left unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmet describes a demand or need that has not been fulfilled, i.e. not satisfied.

clue.text: Air sounds freaked out such old fogeys

indicators.note: someone freaked out is agitated and thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stuffy elderly people alarmed by the noise of a modern tune or jets overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosaurs is a figurative label for people who are hopelessly old-fashioned and resistant to change.

clue.text: Current source of master's trendy interior

indicators.note: interior says the preceding word sits on the inside of the other

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, with the possessive s
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Where a schoolmaster's fashionable home décor gets its power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is electrical, not up to date: the mains is the supply.
explanation.definitionFit: The mains is the main electricity supply to a building, the source of its current.

clue.text: Artificial servant picked up after staff

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the other one

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a maid is a female servant

explanation.surface: A servant is collected after the rest of the household staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Man-made things are produced by people rather than nature, so they are artificial.

clue.text: Case has one placed in clear folder?

indicators.note: placed in puts one piece inside the other word

parts.note: patent means obvious or clear
I is the Roman numeral one
surface padding: a case is also a folder, so the question mark winks at a case file

explanation.surface: A document wallet holding one sheet inside a transparent folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear folder' suggests office stationery, and 'folder?' nods to a case file; the definition is a medical case.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's case is a person under treatment, which is what a patient is.
